title: Normality and properness of an existing finite geometric quotient
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a normal proper finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let a finite group $H$ act on $X$ over $k$. Here normal means that each local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Suppose a $k$-scheme $Z$ and an $H$-invariant morphism of $k$-schemes $q:X\to Z$ (compatible with the structure morphisms to $\operatorname{Spec}k$) are already given such that $q$ is finite and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism], its geometric fibres are $H$-orbits, and $\mathcal O_Z=(q_*\mathcal O_X)^H$ (sections are precisely the invariant sections). Suppose also that every invariant morphism of $k$-schemes from $X$ to a $k$-scheme factors uniquely through $q$ by a morphism of $k$-schemes. Then $Z$ is normal and proper of finite type over $k$, and is Noetherian (it has a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]). Neither the existence of a quotient nor an ample sheaf or projective embedding on $Z$ is asserted. The group action may be nonfaithful and $X$ may be empty or disconnected.

source.place: Agent-formulated general prerequisite for the existing quotients in Expose X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.151. Algebraic finite-type input: Stacks algebra.tex Tag 00IS (Artin--Tate); properness inputs: morphisms.tex Tags 09MQ(4) (separated target of a finite surjection) and 03GN (universally closed image). Normality follows by invariant subrings of the normal domain factors on a finite affine inverse image. This statement does not assert projective quotient existence or projectivity.

proof.text: Write $a:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $b:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ for the structure morphisms, so $bq=a$. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$, and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has its one affine Noetherian chart. The finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem therefore makes $X$ Noetherian. Also $X$ is quasi-compact by finite type. To see that $Z$ is quasi-compact, pull any open cover back along $q$, choose a finite subcover of $X$, and use surjectivity to see that the corresponding opens cover $Z$. Choose a finite affine open cover $Z=\bigcup_j V_j$. This includes the empty cover when $X=Z=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); the cover argument is elementary.

proof.text: For each $V_j=\operatorname{Spec}A_j$, finiteness of $q$ gives $U_j=q^{-1}(V_j)=\operatorname{Spec}B_j$ with $B_j$ finite as an $A_j$-module. The affine-pair characterization of local finite type, applied to $a$ and the affine open $U_j\subset X$, makes $B_j$ a finite-type $k$-algebra. Since $q$ is invariant, $U_j$ is $H$-stable; inverse pullback on sections defines a left action by $k$-algebra automorphisms on $B_j$. The assumed equality of structure sheaves identifies $A_j$ with $B_j^H\subset B_j$, as a $k$-subalgebra (the structure maps agree because $bq=a$). Artin--Tate, with Noetherian base $k$, now makes $A_j$ a finite-type $k$-algebra; the finite-type-algebra Noetherian theorem makes it Noetherian. The finite affine cover from step 1 proves that $b$ is of finite type, by its definition, and that $Z$ has a finite affine cover by Noetherian rings.

source.place: Tag 01WH (definition-integral), finite clause; Tag 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize); algebra.tex Tags 00IS (lemma-Artin-Tate) and 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence).

proof.text: Fix a chart from step 2 and abbreviate its rings to $A=B^H$. The scheme $X$ is locally Noetherian by step 1 and all its stalks are integrally closed domains by hypothesis. The affine open $U=q^{-1}(V)$ is quasi-compact. Apply the normal-section-ring decomposition to this $X$ and $U$ to obtain a ring isomorphism $B\cong\prod_{i\in I}B_i$, with $I$ finite and every $B_i$ an integrally closed domain. Transport the $H$-action to this product. For $U=\varnothing$ the lemma gives $I=\varnothing$ and $B=0$.

source.place: Tags 033N (lemma-normal-locally-Noetherian) and 0358 (lemma-normal-integral-sections); the cited DAG node supplies the full finite-product conclusion, including the empty open.

proof.text: For each $i\in I$, let $e_i$ be the product idempotent equal to $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. In a domain an idempotent $e$ satisfies $e(e-1)=0$, hence is $0$ or $1$. Thus the nonzero idempotents in $B$ which cannot be split into two nonzero orthogonal idempotents are exactly the $e_i$. Every ring automorphism preserves this description, so $H$ permutes the $e_i$, giving an action on $I$. Multiplication by $e_i$ identifies the factor $B_i$ with the ideal $e_iB$, with unit $e_i$. Restriction of $h$ therefore gives a ring isomorphism $h_i:B_i\to B_{hi}$. These satisfy $(gh)_i=g_{hi}h_i$ because they are restrictions of the original action.

source.place: Elementary product-ring calculation; cf. Tag 00EE (lemma-disjoint-decomposition). This step proves the needed idempotent permutation directly.

proof.text: Choose one representative $i$ of each orbit in the finite set $I$, and put $H_i=\{h:hi=i\}$ and $C_i=B_i^{H_i}$. Projection to the representative coordinates gives a ring isomorphism $B^H\cong\prod_{i\in I/H}C_i$. Indeed a fixed tuple must satisfy $x_{hi}=h_i(x_i)$, so the representative coordinates determine it and lie in $C_i$. Conversely, for $c_i\in C_i$, prescribe $x_{hi}=h_i(c_i)$ on that orbit. If $hi=h'i$, then $h^{-1}h'\in H_i$, so the prescription is independent of the choice of $h$. The identity $(gh)_i=g_{hi}h_i$ proves that this tuple is fixed by every $g$. These two constructions are inverse and preserve addition, multiplication and units coordinatewise. For $I=\varnothing$ they are the unique isomorphism of zero rings.

source.place: Agent-written algebraic orbit calculation, expanding the component/stabilizer reduction in Expose X 2.3 Step 3, printed pp.151--152; the full inverse formula and its well-definedness are written here.

proof.text: Each $C_i\subset B_i$ is an integrally closed domain. It is a domain as a unital subring of a domain. To prove integral closedness, take $y=c/d\in\operatorname{Frac}(C_i)$ with $d\ne0$, satisfying a monic equation over $C_i$. Embed this fraction field into $\operatorname{Frac}(B_i)$. The same equation makes $y$ integral over $B_i$, so $y\in B_i$ by its integral closedness. For $h\in H_i$, apply $h_i$ to $dy=c$ in $B_i$; since $c,d$ are fixed, $d h_i(y)=c=dy$. Cancellation of $d\ne0$ gives $h_i(y)=y$. Thus $y\in C_i$, as required. This uses neither faithfulness nor division by $|H_i|$.

source.place: Tag 0309 (definition-domain-normal); elementary monic-equation and cancellation argument, written by the worker for the stabilizer fixed subrings.

proof.text: Each $C_i$ is also a normal ring in the prime-localization sense. For a prime $\mathfrak p\subset C_i$, the localization $(C_i)_{\mathfrak p}$ is a domain inside $\operatorname{Frac}(C_i)$. If $y$ in that field satisfies $y^d+\sum_{r<d}a_r y^r=0$ with $a_r\in(C_i)_{\mathfrak p}$ and $d\ge1$, choose a common denominator $s\in C_i\setminus\mathfrak p$ so that every $sa_r\in C_i$. Then $sy$ satisfies the monic equation $T^d+\sum_{r<d}s^{d-r}a_rT^r=0$ over $C_i$. Step 6 gives $sy\in C_i$, hence $y\in(C_i)_{\mathfrak p}$. This proves integral closedness at every prime, exactly the definition of a normal ring.

source.place: Tag 00GY (lemma-localize-normal-domain), its explicit common-denominator proof; no localization-normality theorem is being used without proof.

proof.text: The finite-product normality theorem applied to the normal rings $C_i$ proves that $\prod_i C_i$ is a normal ring. By the ring isomorphism of step 5, $A$ is normal: a ring isomorphism transports prime ideals, fractions and monic equations, so its prime localizations are integrally closed domains. The affine-open stalk-localization theorem identifies $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ with $(A_j)_{\mathfrak p_z}$ for every $z\in V_j$. Consequently every local ring of $Z$ is an integrally closed domain, proving normality. The zero ring has no primes, so the empty case is included.

source.place: Tag 0CYA (lemma-finite-product-normal); schemes.tex Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), together with the open-subspace stalk identification of Example 01HF, as fully stated by the cited affine-open node.

proof.text: Finally, $q$ is proper because it is finite, and in particular is universally closed. It is surjective by hypothesis. Since $a$ is proper it is separated and universally closed. Apply separatedness descent along the surjective universally closed $q$, over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, to obtain separatedness of $b$. Apply universally-closed-image descent to $bq=a$ to obtain universal closedness of $b$. Together with the finite type already proved in step 2, these properties make $b$ proper. Step 2 also supplies precisely the asserted Noetherian conclusion. All descent hypotheses hold for the empty schemes too. The given geometric-orbit and categorical properties are compatible additional hypotheses; this argument only needs the finite surjection and the invariant-section equality.
